newsitem.title: DENMARK: A.P.Moeller sees 600 mln DKK insurance windfall.
newsitem.headline: A.P.Moeller sees 600 mln DKK insurance windfall.

text.p: Danish shipping group A.P. Moeller said on Monday that it expected its share of a liquidated state insurance fund against war risks for shipping to amount to about 600 million crowns.
The money is expected to be received in 1998.
The fund, set up in 1949, was built up from government contributions and levies on shipowners, of which the Moeller group was the largest in the scheme.

Its liquidation was planned as part of the 1997 budget package and was given final approval by parliament on Friday. The state is expected to receive about 2.3 billion crowns from the winding up of the fund.
Shipowners are henceforth to arrange their own war risks insurance commercially, which smaller operators say will cost them more than the government scheme.

Moeller competitor J.Lauritzen said on Monday that it expected to receive a repayment of about 60 million crowns and Lauritzen's DFDS ferry unit said separately that it estimated its own share as an additional 200 million. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
